knowledge-base.overview: Rocket 0.5+ guardrails, request guard patterns, fairings (middleware), macro-based routing, state management, form handling, and testing for type-safe Rust web APIs. Loaded automatically when agents work on .rs files importing rocket.

core-principles.principle: Attribute macros (#[get], #[post]) enforce method and path at compile time. Dynamic segments are type-checked automatically.
Implement FromRequest for authentication, authorization, and request validation. Guards compose cleanly and fail fast before the handler runs.
Use the Fairing trait for cross-cutting concerns: logging, CORS, request timing. Attach with .attach() at build time.
Use rocket::State<T> for shared application state. Register with .manage() at build time.
Register #[catch(N)] functions for common HTTP error codes to ensure consistent error responses.

guardrail.rule: Never use unwrap() or expect() in handler code, request guards, or fairings. Always handle Result and Option explicitly — return Outcome::Error or an AppError.
Never store secrets in Rocket.toml. Use environment variables for JWT secrets, API keys, and credentials. Reference via std::env::var or Rocket's secret_key mechanism.
Forget to attach the database pool and it will silently fail at runtime. Always .attach(DbPool::init()) in the build function before mounting routes.
Register catchers for 401, 404, and 500 at minimum. Without catchers, Rocket returns default HTML error pages that expose framework details.
Never ignore validation errors from form or JSON input. Use #[field(validate = ...)] in FromForm structs or validate manually in handlers. Failing validation must return a 400/422 response.
Implement Responder for all custom error types. Error types returned from handlers must produce structured JSON responses with appropriate HTTP status codes.

Use Outcome::Error (not Outcome::Forward) when a request guard fails authentication. Forwarding silently falls through to the next matching route, which is almost never the correct behavior for auth failures.
Never block async handlers with synchronous operations. Use tokio::task::spawn_blocking for CPU-bound or blocking I/O work.
Set JSON and form size limits in Rocket.toml. Default limits prevent large payload abuse: limits = { json = "1 MiB", form = "64 kB" }.

project-structure.description: Feature-organized Rocket project: routes mount handlers, guards enforce auth, fairings handle cross-cutting concerns.
project-structure.example: myproject/ ├── Cargo.toml ├── Rocket.toml # Per-profile configuration (debug/release) ├── src/ │ ├── main.rs # #[launch] entry point │ ├── lib.rs # Public module exports │ ├── routes/ │ │ ├── mod.rs # Route mounting functions (returns Vec<Route>) │ │ ├── users.rs # User handlers │ │ └── health.rs # Health check handler │ ├── models/ │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ └── user.rs # Domain types + request/response DTOs │ ├── guards/ # Request guards (auth, admin, rate-limit) │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ └── auth.rs # AuthUser, AdminUser FromRequest impls │ ├── fairings/ # Cross-cutting middleware (CORS, logging, timing) │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ └── logging.rs │ ├── db/ │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ └── pool.rs # DbPool definition (rocket_db_pools) │ ├── services/ # Business logic layer │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ └── user_service.rs │ ├── error.rs # AppError + Responder impl + catchers │ └── config.rs # AppConfig extraction from Rocket.toml / env ├── tests/ │ └── api_tests.rs # Integration tests via rocket::local::asynchronous::Client └── migrations/

configuration.example:
# Rocket.toml [default] address = "0.0.0.0" port = 8000 workers = 16 keep_alive = 5 log_level = "normal" limits = { form = "64 kB", json = "1 MiB" }
[default.databases.db_pool] url = "postgres://user:password@localhost/mydb" min_connections = 5 max_connections = 20 connect_timeout = 5 idle_timeout = 300
[debug] log_level = "debug"
[release] secret_key = "${ROCKET_SECRET_KEY}" # set via environment log_level = "critical"

request-guards.description: Request guards implement FromRequest and run before handlers. Compose guards for role-based access.

error-handling.description: Implement Responder for AppError. Register catchers for all common HTTP error codes.

fairings.description: Fairings attach cross-cutting behavior to the request/response lifecycle using the Fairing trait.

database.description: Use rocket_db_pools for managed database connections. DbConn is a request guard itself.

testing.stack: rocket::local::asynchronous::Client for integration tests; test all routes, guards, and catchers

rules.rule: Use rocket::local::asynchronous::Client for async integration tests
Create a test Rocket instance with a test database via TestPropertyProvider pattern
Test request guards independently by calling from_request with mock request contexts
Test catchers by sending requests that trigger 404, 401, 500 responses
Verify response status codes and JSON body structure in every test
